rows.claim: ArmaturaSec d.o.o. is a 67-person cybersecurity company based in Zrenjanin, founded in 2008.
ArmaturaSec builds OT-focused network security hardware and products including ProtoSense, NetGuard-OT, and NetGuard-OT Mini.
ArmaturaSec’s challenge is to detect unusual behaviour on Modbus and BACnet networks without labelled attack data, using site-specific normal traffic and on-device inference.
ArmaturaSec has collected several terabytes of normal traffic captures from consenting clients over the past three years.
ArmaturaSec can dedicate one to two engineers part-time to a collaborative project and provide traffic archives, a hardware bench, and firmware code under NDA.
Radovan Čičić is ArmaturaSec’s head of engineering.
Krisztina Kiss is a Full Professor in the Faculty of Technical Sciences, Department of Computing and Control Engineering.

Krisztina Kiss’s expertise includes industrial cybersecurity, network traffic analysis, machine learning and statistical modelling, industrial control systems, anomaly detection, one-class classification, SCADA security, statistical baseline modelling, Modbus, DNP3, unsupervised learning, network intrusion detection, and protocol traffic analysis.
Krisztina Kiss’s group has an ICS testbed with Siemens-compatible PLCs, Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators, and packet capture infrastructure.
Krisztina Kiss has collaborated with a regional energy distributor and a water utility on funded projects and consulted for a mid-size automation integrator on SCADA anomaly detection requirements.

Veljko Savić is an Associate Professor in the Faculty of Technical Sciences, Department of Production Engineering.
Veljko Savić works in Production and Industrial Engineering, Maintenance Engineering and Reliability, Biomass Processing Technology, and Applied Statistics and Stochastic Modelling.

His expertise includes condition-based and predictive maintenance for biomass densification equipment, reliability and failure modelling of pellet mills and briquetting presses, wear and degradation analysis, condition monitoring, and stochastic/statistical modelling for maintenance decision support.
Suncokret Eko d.o.o. is a cleantech company focused on biomass and organic waste valorisation.
Suncokret Eko d.o.o. has 31 employees and was founded in 2017.
Suncokret Eko d.o.o. is based in Novi Sad.

Suncokret Eko d.o.o. produces wood-free biomass pellets from sunflower husks and maize cobs, agricultural biochar, custom pelletising services, bulk biochar supply, and carbon-removal documentation support.

Suncokret Eko d.o.o. operates rotary drum drying, hammer-mill size reduction, flat-die and ring-die pellet presses, a slow-pyrolysis reactor, in-line NIR moisture sensing, and ISO 17225 pellet quality testing.

Suncokret Eko d.o.o. has two technically trained staff for controlled production trials and detailed logs, but no dedicated research personnel or laboratory equipment beyond basic moisture and proximate-analysis tools.
The company’s challenge is that the pellet press breaks down about once a month because sunflower husk feedstock has inconsistent moisture and particle size; each incident costs about 15,000 EUR.

The company’s current intake situation includes moisture from 8% to 22%, particle size from fine powder to chunks above 15 mm, clogs above 14% moisture, unreliable NIR below 10% and above 18%, and no automated particle-size check.
The company is considering a secondary hammer mill and a conditioning mixer but has not confirmed whether these would stabilize output enough to prevent failures.

Goran Radulović is an Associate Professor in the Faculty of Technology, Department of Applied and Engineering Chemistry.
Radulović’s expertise includes analytical chemistry, environmental chemistry, water quality monitoring, field analysis, and portable instrumentation.
His research profile includes portable photometric methods for groundwater and water-quality monitoring.
His research profile includes matrix interference correction in colorimetric field analysis.
His research profile includes iron determination and iron speciation in alkaline groundwater.
His research profile includes phosphate analysis and interference from hardness and dissolved organic matter.
Kristal Voda is a water quality testing and on-site treatment equipment company in Zrenjanin.
Kristal Voda has 9 employees and was founded in 2011.
Kristal Voda supplies and maintains water softeners, UV disinfection units, and portable water-quality testing kits for food industry clients across central and southern Vojvodina.
Kristal Voda’s portable turbidity and nitrate kits were specified for water up to about 300 mg/L CaCO₃ hardness.
The challenge samples can exceed 450 mg/L CaCO₃ and sometimes reach 550 mg/L CaCO₃ hardness.
In those samples, turbidity reads 20 to 30 percent higher than the reference lab and nitrate can read low by a similar margin.
The company wants a fast, on-site, handheld solution and cannot budget reference-lab testing for every field sample.
